answer: Paragraph 14 most naturally makes confirmation unconditional on an SFC request and demonstration request-triggered. Both concern management and operational soundness, ownership record keeping and smart-contract integrity; demonstration must satisfy the SFC. Footnote 5 specifies minimum content—compliance with paragraphs 10–13 and high confidence concerning absence of smart-contract vulnerabilities or security flaws—but repeats “confirm and demonstrate” without a request qualification. This supports a rival standing-demonstration reading, although reading the footnote as specifying the content of the request-triggered demonstration better preserves paragraph 14’s express condition. Without a request, confirmation remains applicable; demonstration is untriggered under the integrated reading but remains applicable under the standing-footnote reading. Neither conclusion establishes fulfillment. Paragraphs 15 and 16 separately condition obtaining third-party audit or verification and a satisfactory legal opinion on the relevant SFC request.

claims.inference: Text and grammatical deduction: the inserted request condition attaches to “demonstrate”; “to the SFC’s satisfaction” directly qualifies demonstration. The shared objects follow both verbs. Footnote 5 expressly identifies the SFC as recipient of confirmation as well.
missing_premises: Applicability of this retained edition to the Product Provider, product, activity and assessment interval, including any applicable conditions or amendments.
Actual confirmation and its content; evidence sufficient to assess fulfillment.
Any applicable clarification determining whether the SFC-satisfaction standard also governs confirmation.
claims.proposition: Paragraph 14 separates confirmation from request-triggered demonstration concerning the same three subjects.

support.quote: Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.
Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC

claims.inference: Text: the footnote supplies a minimum object for both verbs. Its high-confidence wording concerns the proposition about smart-contract vulnerabilities or security flaws; it is not a numerical threshold and does not expressly replace the main text’s SFC-satisfaction standard. Judgment: integrating this content with paragraph 14 preserves both provisions, but the footnote’s omission of the request condition leaves a supported rival reading.
missing_premises: An authoritative resolution of whether footnote 5 carries forward paragraph 14’s request condition.
An applicable evidential standard for “high level of confidence” and “SFC’s satisfaction”.
Evidence of compliance with paragraphs 10–13 and the condition of the relevant smart contracts.
claims.proposition: Footnote 5 specifies minimum confirmation and demonstration content, while leaving a tension over demonstration’s trigger.

support.quote: 5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.
upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction

claims.inference: Conditional deduction assuming no applicable request was made: under readings A and C, demonstration is not triggered; under reading B, footnote demonstration remains standing. Confirmation survives on each reading. Absence of a request supplies no evidence that confirmation or the underlying substantive requirements have been fulfilled.
missing_premises: Reliable facts establishing that no applicable SFC request covers the activity and interval.
Resolution of the rival demonstration readings.
Actual performance evidence and applicable fulfillment standards.
claims.proposition: No request does not remove confirmation or establish substantive compliance; its effect on demonstration depends on the retained reading.

support.quote: Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate
Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above

Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

claims.inference: Text and deduction: each provision conditions its own obtaining requirement on an SFC request. Paragraph 15 concerns third-party audit or verification of the three specified subjects; paragraph 16 concerns a satisfactory legal opinion supporting the application. A request for paragraph 14 demonstration does not by itself establish either other trigger, although a single request could expressly cover multiple requirements.
missing_premises: The terms, scope and timing of any SFC request.
For fulfillment, the obtained audit, verification or legal opinion and evidence that it meets the applicable scope and standard.
Any independent audit or opinion requirement applicable outside these provisions.
claims.proposition: Paragraphs 15 and 16 have distinct request-triggered acts and objects; without their relevant requests, these provisions do not themselves trigger obtaining those materials.

support.quote: Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain third party audit or verification on the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and integrity of the smart contracts.
Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain satisfactory legal opinion to support its application.

rival_readings: A — Main-text reading: demonstration of paragraph 14’s three subjects is triggered by an SFC request and must satisfy the SFC; the precise incorporation of footnote 5’s object and standard remains unresolved.

B — Standing-footnote reading: footnote 5’s unqualified “confirm and demonstrate” creates a standing demonstration requirement with its stated minimum content and high-confidence smart-contract standard. This reading must explain its tension with the express main-text request condition.

C — Integrated reading: footnote 5 specifies minimum content for confirmation and for demonstration when requested; demonstration remains subject to SFC satisfaction, with the high-confidence smart-contract requirement included. This is the stronger textual reconciliation, not an established authoritative resolution.
unresolved: The retained sources do not conclusively resolve the main-text/footnote trigger tension or the reach of the SFC-satisfaction standard over confirmation.
The sources do not prescribe a numerical confidence threshold or a complete evidential test for fulfillment.
No assessed entity, applicable request history, actual confirmation, demonstration or performance evidence is supplied.

Applicability, additional conditions and any relevant amendments require assessment for the actual interval. Candidate rules, Boolean readings and graph acceptance cannot establish legal truth or fulfillment.
